newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: John Keells brews rich profit from tea.
newsitem.headline: John Keells brews rich profit from tea.

text.p: A sharp rise in profit of the Sri Lankan conglomerate John Keells, which announced its results on Monday, was led by a boom in tea plus food and beverages businesses, analysts said.
John Keells said that its profits for year to March 1997 rose 27 percent to 421 million rupees on a turnover of 5.72 billion rupees.
"Growth has been led by John Keells' plantation holdings and its food and beverage firms, which have also performed well," said Mahendra Jayasekera, general manager of brokerage CT Smith.
John Keells has controlling interests in Kegalle Plantations Ltd, Tea Smallholder Factories Ltd and the yet to be listed Maskeliya Plantations Ltd.
Analysts said profits of John Keells, one of the leading commodity brokers in the island nation, were also pushed up by buoyant tea prices.
Tea prices reached a record high in 1996 due to heavy demand from the Commonwealth of Independent States and the Middle East, with the national sales average of a kilo of tea rising to 103.88 rupees.

"The bulk of the group's profits have definitely come from plantations, and we are revising upwards forecasts for the year ended 31 March, 1998," said Panduka Ambanpola, head of research at brokerage Jardine Fleming HNB.

"At the current price of 225 rupees a 10-rupee share, the scrip is trading at about 17 times March 31, 1998 forecast earnings," he said. "It will be far more attractive after we have made an upward revision of our profit forecasts for the next financial yer," he added.
Analsyts said the group's two food and beverage subsidiaries Ceylon Cold Stores and Keells Food Products have also done well and contributed their fair share to profitablity.
"The upturn we have seen so far in tourism would have also enhanced earnings," said Jayaskera.
The state Ceylon Tourist Board recently said arrivals in the first quarter of 1997 were 17 percent up from a year earlier, compred with an overall decline of 25 percent in 1996.
John Keells Holdings is the largest tour operator into Sri Lanka.
